extracted.intended_audience: independent documentary filmmakers applying to the Sundance Documentary Fund
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting feature-length nonfiction documentary project proposals to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, including eligibility, required materials, evaluation standards, and application process rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artful or innovative film language
rubrics_metrics.description: Support independent nonfiction films that display artful film language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed explicitly as one of the primary evaluation dimensions. Implies attention to cinematic craft and form; Sundance also notes they fund hybrid/animated and experimental documentaries, and look for innovation in form (e.g., purely historical/biographical films are less likely to be funded unless they show innovation in form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear storytelling / Story Summary quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The story summary should convey the film's story and story structure, describing primary characters/subjects, their potential journey, the mission, stakes, central question and possible outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must articulate story and structure; projects that cannot articulate characters, story or the driving central question are discouraged. The story summary may also describe important artistic elements or creative approaches. Reviewers evaluate 'clear storytelling' as a core criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are evaluated for originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Fund's evaluation rubric (originality listed alongside artful language, storytelling, feasibility, cultural relevance, and audience reach). The FAQ also warns they 'tend not to fund purely historical or biographical films unless they show clear contemporary relevance, or innovation in form,' indicating originality/novel approach increases competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (project viability & budgeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project is feasible and the production plan is realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit a 1-2 page comprehensive line-item budget in US dollars covering the entire project from development through distribution. The written proposal should include a fundraising strategy that distinguishes between funds applied for and funds already secured. Feasibility is an explicit evaluation dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary cultural relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate what is timely and significant about your project and how stakes matter beyond primary characters to broader audiences or contemporary cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAQ defines this term: explain why the project matters now and its broader cultural stakes. Sundance tends not to fund strictly historical/biographical work unless it demonstrates clear contemporary relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to reach and connect with intended audience (distribution & engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the project's potential to reach and connect with its intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide a Distribution/Marketing Strategy—an outline of intended festival, theatrical, broadcast, home video, or educational distribution, and concrete explanation of the best outlets for the film. Also distinguish distribution (placing film on screens) from Audience Engagement (campaigns to activate audiences/stakeholders). For series, proposals should demonstrate especially concrete and specific plans for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be feature-length documentaries (52 minutes and longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid/animated and experimental documentaries are eligible. The Fund does NOT fund fiction films or standalone short films (shorts have a separate Shorts Fund). If you live in a region with internet-access issues, contact Documentary Film Program for exceptions to sample delivery rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible subject matter / film types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund does not support fiction films, standalone short films, strictly historical or biographical films (unless they show contemporary relevance or form innovation), NGO films, or educational films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit exclusions: 'We do not fund NGO, or educational films.' They also generally do not fund purely historical/biographical films unless they show clear contemporary relevance or innovation in form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing & project stage for application
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit only when you can demonstrate creative and storytelling intent; may apply at any production phase from development through post-production but not after a premiere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to apply at least 6 months before an anticipated premiere. Projects without secured characters, a clear story/structure, or a driving central question are discouraged. The Fund cannot consider proposals for story research. Picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding and once a film premieres, Sundance cannot provide post-production support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample format and delivery requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All visual samples must be submitted as online streaming links (recommended: Vimeo), not as file transfer services or DVDs (except by special DVD exemption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an online streaming link and password; make the film downloadable and available for at least 6 months after submission. Do not update/change the uploaded file or its password after submission. Do not use WeTransfer, Dropbox, or other file-transfer services. DVDs are not accepted unless an exemption is granted for countries with significant impediments to internet access (email DFP@sundance.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample accessibility and password rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the streaming link and password work and are correctly entered in the application and proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passwords are case sensitive—double-check entry. If Sundance cannot access the file/password they will not be able to evaluate the project. Include the Vimeo link and password in both the application form and the written proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior directing sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A visual sample that conveys the director's storytelling ability is preferred as the prior directing sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is a directorial debut, you may submit a film you have shot or edited, or a previous work from a key creative member of the team (e.g., editor, cinematographer). Completed prior work may be any length and any genre but must be submitted in its entirety; reviewers will only make time to review one sample. Do not submit segments of different projects on one reel. If you have multiple prior works or co-directors, select one that best reflects the vision for the new documentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample length and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Length/quality of production samples affects category placement and competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production/post-production proposals with very short reels (or only trailers, teasers, or brief selects) are not competitive against longer rough cuts and will be bumped down to the development category. If you lack a 10-minute sample, you may apply in the development category or wait until you have necessary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written proposal language and currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be written in English and budgets translated into U.S. dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund can only consider proposals written in English, with visual material in English or with English subtitles/transcript. Budgets must be provided in USD; a sample budget/template is available on the Sundance website and may be adapted to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising strategy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a fundraising strategy that explains plans to raise the film budget and clearly distinguishes between funds applied for and funds already secured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include potential sources such as foundations, broadcast license agreements, private donations, in-kind support, crowdfunding, producer investment, and fundraisers. The written proposal should include this strategy regardless of whether prior funding exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution/marketing strategy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline intended festival, theatrical, broadcast, home video, or educational distribution and concrete steps to reach the intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need secured agreements to include in your strategy, but it should be a concrete explanation of the best outlets for your film and what you will do to have it reach its intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement definition & appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience Engagement is a strategic campaign to move individuals and communities from passive viewers to active participants on the issue the film addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is distinct from distribution and from marketing/outreach; it is designed to activate audiences and stakeholders toward a specific goal. Not all films are necessarily suited for social engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals undergo a multi-stage review with selected submissions sent to the Sundance Documentary Fund Committee; decisions typically take 3–5 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee includes issue-area experts, film artists, and curators. The process is highly competitive (~1,300 proposals/year with 40–60 funded). Applicants should not contact staff for status updates; they will be notified by email when a decision is made. Projects reaching the final stage may be eligible for feedback, but staff cannot provide feedback to all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-application and project advancement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You may reapply only when your project has advanced in storytelling vision and intent and generally after significant further production activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filmmakers are strongly discouraged from resubmitting nearly identical proposals or visual samples. If reapplying, submit a complete, brand-new online application with new video links and materials that reflect substantive development since the last submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit more than one proposal in the same round as long as they are for separate projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proposal must be a distinct project; do not submit multiple entries for the same project in one round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding exclusions related to completion and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund does not fund tape-to-film transfers, film prints, or debt reimbursement; they generally do not provide solely completion funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding. If your project is finished, you cannot apply for funding to pay for film transfers or to reimburse debt used to complete the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant terms and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sundance grants are not recoupable and do not encumber exploitable rights; recipients must meet contract terms and reporting obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract asks for verbal and logo acknowledgement in the end credits and on promotional materials, submission of 4 copies of the finished film on DVD, narrative/financial/distribution reports, and social impact reports if applicable. Sundance may request grantee participation in Institute activities to support the creative community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global eligibility & first-time filmmaker policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent filmmakers from anywhere in the world are welcome to apply; first-time filmmakers are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Films may be in any language provided there are English subtitles or a transcript. Prior funding, fiscal sponsorship, and American producers are not required for eligibility.
